covers.title: The Cloud That Shared Its Rain
covers.prompt: Vertical full-bleed children’s science-storybook cover. On a river road above Bellwether Village, eight-year-old Mina in a bright red raincoat, red scarf, yellow boots, and field notebook stands beneath a huge silver-gray cloud, holding an open red umbrella as cool rain falls on the bakery roof, blue pond, cracked brown fields, and leaves below. Shape one clear vertical water-cycle journey through the scene: warm sunlight illuminates the river, invisible water-vapor wisps rise into the cool air, tiny droplets gather inside the cloud, rain descends, and a shining gutter carries water back toward the river. Mina reaches one hand into the rain with quiet wonder as neighbors collect it, expressing the emotional resolution that the cloud is part of a cycle, not a creature giving gifts. Cool blue-gray and white with vivid red and emerald accents, rounded readable forms, luminous watercolor-and-gouache, expressive natural faces, clear focal hierarchy. No rendered text, letters, numbers, labels, captions, or logos.

Nia’s realization that light energy powers sugar and new growth is the emotional focus. covers.title: Why the Sky Said Blue
covers.prompt: Vertical full-bleed children’s science-fantasy cover on the hill above a small town. Nine-year-old Pella in a mustard shirt and sturdy boots stands highest at a giant clear-glass Prism Bell, opening its shutters to a brilliant white sunbeam. Show the phenomenon in one readable vertical arc: a white beam enters the bell, short-wavelength blue light scatters broadly through the surrounding air to create a deep blue overhead sky, while the remaining light reaches the red barn and river below as pale white sunlight. Near the distant horizon the same low-angle sunlight travels through a longer air path and warms to gold, orange, and coral at sunset. Pella holds a brass spyglass and smiles with quiet triumph, her face and the bell forming the focal point; the blue sky fills the upper half and her now-responsible position below resolves the mystery. covers.title: The Magnet with Two Moods
covers.prompt: Vertical full-bleed children’s science-storybook cover at a rain-speckled school-fair booth. Nine-year-old Niko in a yellow raincoat and red boots holds a red-and-blue bar magnet above a cereal-box test tray, smiling with satisfaction as steel paper clips leap toward one pole and a second magnet snaps away; his eight-year-old sister Luma in a green hood records the fair result in an open notebook. Curved black iron filings across white paper reveal the magnetic-field pattern, dense near the poles and spreading farther away, while Dr. Moss in a green utility vest lifts an iron nail wrapped with a copper-wire coil connected to a battery and switch, showing the electromagnet that releases the clip when the switch opens. Keep Niko, Luma, the two magnet ends, and the filings crisp in the foreground; the mystery is resolved through fair tests rather than a magical mood. Bright red, blue, copper, and rain gray, lively but readable watercolor-and-gouache, expressive natural faces, strong vertical hierarchy. covers.title: The Bridge That Counted Forces
covers.prompt: Vertical cinematic young-adult science-adventure cover. A newly rebuilt wooden footbridge with clear triangular side trusses spans the deep brown flood between mossy banks, its joints and iron pegs visibly locked. Eleven-year-old Mira in red boots and a mustard coat stands highest at the survey board, calmly marking the safe load; twelve-year-old Oren in a blue sweater braces a diagonal member, and nine-year-old Tavi in a green waterproof jacket tests a final joint as four identical sandbags press down near the center. Make the force path clear through the composition: the load travels through the deck, pulling tension along one diagonal while compressing another, then into end posts and the ground; the stable triangles prevent racking, answering the broken first bridge folded by shear. In the lower background, villagers cross safely at sunset while the flood carries leaves onward, giving the scene an earned, cooperative resolution. Warm wood against storm blue and muddy water, adventurous painterly realism, crisp structural lines, expressive determined faces, strong vertical depth. covers.title: The Forest That Shared Its Meals
covers.prompt: Vertical cinematic ecological-adventure cover in Lanternwood forest at dawn. Eleven-year-old Nia in a mustard field vest kneels at the largest focal point, holding a pale deer antler and field notebook beside clipped willow shoots, a deer trail, fungi, and a visible food-web pattern woven through the scene. A deer browses at one side, while a gray wolf and a darker wolf remain at a respectful distance on the forest path behind her; wildlife officer Mara in a green utility jacket points out a paw print while Nia’s classmate Tovan watches from a fern-covered slope. Shape a layered, non-linear food web rather than a simple predator chain: sunlit green plants feed several herbivores, predators connect to different animals, fungi and bacteria receive fallen matter, and luminous nutrient threads return through soil to roots while usable energy flows one way. At the bottom, a protective woven fence surrounds intact young saplings, resolving the town’s conflict with caution, observation, and habitat protection. Moss green, earthy brown, gray fur, and warm sunrise gold, painterly realism, clear age-safe focal hierarchy, rich vertical forest depth. covers.title: The Star That Built Its Own Light
covers.prompt: Vertical cinematic science-fantasy cover split along one continuous visual axis between a moonlit sea cliff and the interior of a star. At the lower center, twelve-year-old Neri Vale in a navy field coat and rust boots turns the crank of an old Listening Tower while astronomer aunt Mara steadies a giant mirror and prism. The gathered ninety-three-year-old starlight enters a broad silver beam, guides the endangered fishing boat Wren through fog, and rises through the upper half into a cutaway stellar interior. There, immense golden gravity pulls inward, blue-white gas pressure pushes outward, and four glowing hydrogen nuclei at the bright core join step by step into helium, releasing a burst of light and heat; countless shorter zigzag paths show photons repeatedly absorbed and re-emitted before energy diffuses outward and escapes. Neri’s focused wonder and the rescued boat below provide the emotional resolution: an old signal can still be useful now. Deep navy, silver, white, and molten gold, adventurous age-safe painterly realism, dramatic vertical scale, crisp character silhouettes. covers.title: The Battery That Remembered Charge
covers.prompt: Vertical cinematic science-mystery cover in the battery room of storm-battered Mallow Reef lighthouse. Thirteen-year-old Tamsin in an oversized yellow raincoat and rubber boots leans over a multimeter with a wondering expression; fifteen-year-old Neri in a navy keeper’s vest follows a damp green corrosion path from a cracked cable gland to the steel rack, while keeper Mara Venn in a soaked oilskin checks a correctly matched charger. The six sealed battery cases rise behind them toward the rotating white lighthouse beam, and a small test bulb glows steadily in the foreground. Show the electrochemistry as a clean visual flow rather than a literal cutaway: electrons travel through the external wire from negative to positive, the lamp changes their energy into light and heat, ions balance reactions inside the electrolyte, and a hidden leak path drains current until the clean repair and a weak cell are identified. Tamsin’s realization that chemical potential—not stored electrons or a faulty memory—keeps the light possible provides the emotional resolution. Storm blue-black, steel gray, copper, and warm amber instrument light, investigative age-safe tension, expressive faces, strong vertical depth. covers.title: The Map of a Warming World
covers.prompt: Vertical cinematic climate-science fantasy cover in the highest map tower of the Archive of Coasts. Sixteen-year-old apprentice cartographer Ilyra Venn, in a teal wool cloak over a cream tunic, stands at the center of a floating chart table as a coastal map redraws itself around her; Councilwoman Sera in a white fur-edged coat pauses before signing, and Master Orren steadies a brass energy-balance instrument behind them. Make radiative balance physically legible: golden solar energy enters from above, some is immediately reflected, most warms ocean, land, ice, and living systems, and infrared energy tries to return to space through layers that include greenhouse gases slowing escape. Below the table, a warmer ocean feeds a rotating coastal storm with visible moisture, while along the map edge snow retreats, an orchard blooms early, and a flood gauge rises; behind Ilyra, a layered band of measured past history, projected ranges, and uncertain blank areas replaces erased certainty. The lower scene shows practical responses—wetlands absorbing overflow, strengthened roofs, shaded cooling spaces, wind and solar power, and planned adaptation—while the warming pressure remains visible. Ilyra’s calm refusal to hide uncertainty and the city’s partial preparation form the emotional resolution. Icy cyan, deep navy, parchment cream, and coral-red, sophisticated painterly realism, dramatic vertical scale, restrained but hopeful. No rendered text, letters, numbers, labels, captions, maps with lettering, or logos.

covers.title: The Machine That Learned from Mistakes
covers.prompt: Vertical cinematic machine-learning cover in a storm-lit stone weather tower above Bellwether. Seventeen-year-old Nara Venn, in a navy work jacket and copper goggles, stands highest at a giant brass prediction face with its needle lifted uncertainly; seventy-three-year-old records keeper Sera Holt, in a moss-green field coat, holds a barometer and open weather ledger while Master Iven watches from a bank of copper-threaded calculation boxes. Connect the tower to the town below with visible but nonliteral learning structure: sky sensors feed values through weighted connections, a prediction is compared with observed rain, an error signal travels back to adjust connections, and a separate withheld set of weather remains outside the training path. In the background, a faulty pressure seal, a washed-out practice bridge, and a later rising real river show bad data, overfitting, and genuine uncertainty without turning the machine into a villain. At the bottom, Nara and Sera act on a cautious forecast by closing the bridge, moving seed crates, and helping neighbors before heavy rain arrives, resolving the story through calibrated trust rather than blind reliance or rejection. Storm gray, copper, muted blue, and warm shelter light, sophisticated painterly realism, dense but legible depth, serious hopeful mood. covers.title: The Earthquake Beneath the Mountain
covers.prompt: Vertical cinematic geoscience cover beneath a midnight mountain near an abandoned slate quarry. Geology student Nia Venn, in a rust-red winter jacket and gloves, crouches beside a pulsing blue mineral seam while sixteen-year-old Asha Bell, in a yellow rain shell, steadies a calibrated ground-motion sensor above them; engineer Tomas Rhee and former quarry worker Mr. Petrov watch from the stone observatory doorway. Reveal the mountain as a cutaway system: distant tectonic plates move at fingernail speed, folded rock and a partially locked fault accumulate stress, and a sudden slip sends seismic waves through the valley at different strengths depending on distance and local ground. The blue vein remains mysterious rather than falsely labeled a prediction; calibrated traces, survey pins, a fault map, and observations occupy the foreground, showing that magnitude describes the source while intensity varies by place. In the lower background, workers secure shelves, reinforce the school load path, widen an exit, inspect a bridge and water tank, and residents prepare with drop-cover-hold behavior. After a moderate tremor, the improved school remains open while an unreinforced shop is visibly repaired, resolving the story through measurement and preparation rather than claimed certainty. Midnight navy, ice blue, granite gray, and sharp amber lamplight, sophisticated painterly realism, compelling vertical depth. covers.title: The Edge of the Black Hole
covers.prompt: Vertical cinematic relativistic-rescue cover in deep space. Commander Ilyan Vey, in a white rescue suit with a blue stripe, braces at the airlock of the white Lanterns ship while rescued crewman Teo Rusk, in a cracked spacesuit, reaches through the open lock with one hand; behind them the damaged Aster Vale tilts beyond a blazing accretion disk. Frame the true black center low and central, surrounded by an event horizon that is not a wall: a glowing curved boundary marks the region from which no future path leads outward, while an outside tether and the rescue ship’s carefully timed engine burn keep their route open. Background stars stretch into luminous parentheses around the black hole, and a sequence of increasingly delayed, dimmer, redder flashes from the lost ship visually communicates gravitational redshift and signal travel time. Make the physics and the painful resolution coexist: light emitted outside can still arrive as a history after the vessel crosses, but no new signal can return from inside. Teo is safe while the vanished ship is not, and the crew’s final outward path remains a small beacon of grief and hard-won knowledge. Stark white, electric cyan, gold, deep violet, and absolute black, photoreal space physics, dramatic vertical composition, restrained human emotion, crisp focal hierarchy.
